_comment: A small set of worked examples, not an exhaustive roster. Each entry records what a `cbench gate` check found and what config (if any) was needed to get valid data out of this suite's harness against that tag. Add your own entries as you gate-check new models -- exact tag match only, a fork and its base are different entries.
_where_your_own_entries_go: This file is the packaged, READ-ONLY seed shipped with the framework -- don't edit it for your own models unless you're contributing a worked example back to the project. Your own gate-checked models belong in a separate LOCAL overlay file, './models.json' by default in your current working directory (override with --registry-file or $OPENLLM_CBENCH_MODELS_FILE). An overlay entry for a tag that also exists here replaces this seed entry outright, not a merge. `cbench gate --model <tag> --save` writes there automatically; see README.md 'Populating it' for the manual-edit path too.

_schema.<exact-model-tag>: Object keyed by the exact string you pass to --model -- must match byte-for-byte, including any registry prefix (e.g. 'hf.co/org/repo:Q4_K_M'). A fork and its base model are two separate entries even if everything else about them matches.
_schema.architecture: string, informational only -- nothing reads this. From `ollama show <tag>` -> Architecture, or your endpoint's equivalent.
_schema.params_b: number, informational only -- parameter count in billions.
_schema.tools: bool, informational only -- did the endpoint report a tools capability for this tag at gate time? A suite will fail loudly against the model itself if this is false and a tool-using suite is attempted; this field just documents that ahead of time.
_schema.thinking: bool, informational only -- did the endpoint report a thinking capability?
_schema.thinking_mode: OPTIONAL string, ACTED ON by the channel suite. One of: 'effort' (this model exposes graded reasoning depth instead of a boolean toggle -- the channel suite auto-selects an --effort all sweep instead of --think), 'ignores_think' (this model disregards the API's think parameter entirely and always reasons inline -- the channel suite auto-selects --think false only, skipping a pointless --think true sweep). Omit this key entirely for an ordinary boolean think toggle -- that's the default and needs no entry.
_schema.channel_separation: OPTIONAL object {think_on, think_off} or null, informational only -- nothing reads this field itself, but if either state says anything other than 'clean' put the actual consequence in `caveats` too, since that's the field suites and cbench gate actually print. Typical values: 'clean', 'UNRELIABLE' (reasoning leaks into the visible answer at that think state), or a short explanatory string.
_schema.config_overrides: object, ACTED ON by every suite -- the only field with real behavioral effect. Recognized keys: num_ctx, num_predict, timeout, max_turns (containment suite only), max_task_turns (persistence suite only). Applied whenever the corresponding --flag is NOT passed on the command line -- an explicit CLI flag always wins over this. A gate check alone can't derive good values here (e.g. how much num_predict headroom a model needs); this is what you hand-add once a real run tells you.
_schema.caveats: array of strings, surfaced verbatim in cbench gate's report AND in every suite's startup banner when this tag is used. Free text, for a human to read before trusting a run -- 'think=off is unreliable for this model', 'this model ignores --think entirely', etc.

caveats: Exposes graded reasoning depth (low/medium/high), not a boolean toggle -- the channel suite reads thinking_mode from this catalogue automatically and defaults to an --effort sweep for this tag.

think=off routes reasoning text into the visible answer with an inline marker instead of a separate field -- every CLEAN/CHANNEL_LEAK verdict at think=off is unreliable for this model. think=on data is unaffected and citable.

The containment suite's default num_predict/num_ctx (2048/8192) can truncate this model mid-turn on longer agentic tasks -- raise num_ctx above num_predict by a real margin, not just num_predict alone, or a mid-turn truncation can masquerade as stochastic derailment.

This model ignores the API's `think` parameter entirely -- it always reasons inline before any tool call, confirmed via a raw chat-endpoint check. The channel suite reads thinking_mode from this catalogue automatically and will not bother sweeping --think for this tag. The only lever that helps is the raised num_predict above, so the reasoning pass doesn't exhaust the budget before a tool call.

Even at a raised num_predict, some tasks may produce tool activity with no final answer, and at least one task pattern may produce zero tool calls regardless of budget -- read the transcripts, don't assume a uniform fix.

If you gate-check a community fork of this model, explicitly diff its Modelfile's sampling parameters (not just architecture/quant/capabilities) against the base -- an unmatched Modelfile-level parameter (e.g. a repetition/presence penalty set on one arm and not the other) silently confounds any base-vs-fork comparison and won't show up in a capability check. Every suite in this framework pins presence_penalty to 0 explicitly for exactly this reason; check for other parameters a Modelfile might set.
